releases.title: V4.0.1: every new module now explains itself in hand and on the recipe pages; the Geofracture Drill needs no power
releases.summary: Fixes for the V4.0.0 field report that the 20 new modules gave no clue how to start them. All 20 now carry usage text you read by hovering the item, and the Chronos Anchor, Gravity Inverter and Null-Zone Generator answer with their status when right-clicked with an empty hand. The recipe pages gain all V4 recipes plus a 20-section usage guide. The Geofracture Drill no longer needs power, because a gap-free casing and a touching cable could not both be satisfied.

sections.title: Highlights
items: All 20 modules have hover text explaining how to use them. In V4.0.0, nine machines and gear (Thermodynamic Engine, Aetherial Conduit, Geofracture Drill, Automated Fabricator, Biological Weaver, slag, Resonance Rail, Kinetic Dampening boots, Glitch Strider) had usage text inside the jar that was never displayed, and most of the rest had none at all.

Chronos Anchor, Gravity Inverter and Null-Zone Generator answer an empty-hand right-click with active/idle, what they need, and their region size. The Chronos Anchor starts on a redstone signal (a lever will do) — nothing said so before.
The Geofracture Drill needs no power (config drill.wattsFactor 0 = no power; set it above 0 to require power as before). A 2.0 saved by V4.0.0 is repaired to 0 automatically on start.
The recipe pages on this site now list all 25 V4 recipes and a usage guide for the 20 new modules; its numbers are read from each mod's config.
The Air Purifier (V2) and the train stop's auto-depart hint were hidden by the same cause and are shown now.
A gate that checks, both ways, that every usage text is displayed by code now runs in all 12 modules, so this class of defect stops before packaging.

sections.title: Balance changes
items: Geofracture Drill default power draw: 2 machines → 0 (no power).

sections.title: Warnings
items: Installs straight into an existing world. The drill setting is repaired on start and the config file version becomes 9.
V4 usage is in each item's hover text and on this site's recipe pages under the guide tab: "How to use the 20 new V4 modules".

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: There is no Minecraft client in the development environment, so how the hover text and status lines look has not been checked in-game.
The usage guide is Japanese only, like the existing power guide.

releases.title: The V4 update: 20 new modules, from the Chronos Anchor to the Atmospheric Harvester
releases.summary: V4 is the biggest update this pack has had. Six mods - sky, power, survival, rail, guns and deco - gain 20 modules: an anchor that stops time, a bottomless pouch, a locator that draws sound around you, a mirror onto another dimension, resonance rails, an acoustic turret and more. It installs straight into an existing world; the config files gain the new keys automatically on first start.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Chronos Anchor (sky): while powered, it halts block machinery and creatures in the 5×5×5 around it. Cut the power or break it and everything resumes.
Void-Stitched Pocket (survival): an effectively bottomless carried pouch. It becomes a unique item the first time it is opened, and only loses its contents when it burns in lava.
Echolic Locator (survival): picks up sounds made by nearby hostile and neutral mobs and by players, and draws a line towards each one.
Thermodynamic Engine (power): generates from the biome temperature difference read 8 blocks out in the four directions. No fuel; output scales with the difference, with a cap.
Entropy Siphon (survival): a weapon enchantment (up to III). Repairs your damaged gear by 20% of the victim's max health per level.
Resonance Rail (rail): raises the minecart speed limit only while powered (25 m/s by default, up to 50 m/s in the config) and pre-loads the chunks ahead.
Aetherial Conduit (power): sends items and fluids to any container within 16 blocks. The target is set with the new Aetherial Tuner item; it draws one machine's worth of power.
Kinetic Dampening Matrix (survival): boots that cancel fall damage and release a shockwave on landing, scaled by fall distance (up to 6). They do not break blocks by default.
Photic Synthesiser (deco): a light whose red, green and blue channels are tuned by right-clicking with dyes. At one specific ratio it speeds up the crop directly below.

Geofracture Drill (power): a stationary auto-miner. Enclose it in a 3×3 casing, feed it two machines' worth of power, and it bores a 3×3 face, storing everything in an adjacent container (it waits when full; nothing is lost).
Biological Weaver (power): turns two DNA syringes plus power into a hybrid spawn egg. The mob spawns as parent A's species with parent B's movement speed and attack damage.
Spatial Transpositor (sky): swaps places with a mob up to 32 blocks away. 5-second cooldown.
Gravity Inverter (sky): pushes everything upward in an 8×16×8 region above it; whoever leaves through the top gets slow falling.
Glitch Strider (survival): a four-piece armour set. With the full set, press G to blink 3 blocks along your line of sight, through walls. 1 second of invulnerability, 6-second cooldown.
Acoustic Turret (guns): listens for sound (vibrations) within 16 blocks and fires sonic blasts. It does not target players by default.
Dimensional Mirror (sky): shows the dimension, biome and time of day of a place linked with a lodestone compass, as one of 11 pictures.
Automated Fabricator (power): crafts the recipe laid out in its 3×3 template once a second from materials in adjacent containers. One machine's worth of power.
Sub-Zero Cryo-Cannon (guns): each hit applies a stacking frostbite slow; the fifth stack encases the target in ice.
Null-Zone Generator (sky): inside a 16-block sphere, redstone signal updates and the application of status effects stop. Needs no power.
Atmospheric Harvester (power): under open sky, collects the gas or liquid that matches the biome's temperature and altitude. Needs no power.

sections.title: Balance changes
items: The Resonance Rail's default limit is 25 m/s. The specified 50 m/s is the ceiling you can choose in the config (chunk-loading load).
The Kinetic Dampening boots' shockwave does not break blocks by default; enable it with kineticBootsBreakBlocks.

sections.title: Warnings
items: Installs straight into an existing world. The V4 keys are added to the config files automatically on start.
The G key is shared between the Glitch Strider blink and the rail door / vehicle gear controls. You cannot blink while riding.
The Null Zone refuses every status effect regardless of source - potion, beacon or enchantment (exceptions go in the tag #sorakaze_sky:null_zone_passes). Effects already applied are not removed.
Riding Resonance Rails at speed loads the chunks ahead. If server load rises, lower the speed limit in the config.
The Acoustic Turret reacts to non-player sounds (mob footsteps, attacks and so on). To let it hit players, enable hitsPlayers in the config.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The Dimensional Mirror shows one of 11 pictures chosen from the target's dimension, biome and time of day, not the actual view on the other side.
The Chronos Anchor does not keep scheduled ticks that piled up while frozen when the world is saved.
The Acoustic Turret saves its dish direction, but the model does not rotate.
There is no Minecraft client in the development environment, so the new modules' visuals, sounds and key controls have not been checked in-game.

groups.label: V3.8
groups.summary: The Mining Drill Rig, and anti-materiel damage on every heavy and ranged weapon

releases.title: The Mining Drill Rig, and anti-materiel damage on every heavy and ranged weapon
releases.summary: Adds the Mining Drill Rig: a tracked machine you ride, set down, and drill with. It clears a 5x5 face in one pass and goes through obsidian — in exchange it is very slow and cannot move at all while drilling. The same release lets heavy items, projectiles and ranged weapons damage blocks, with a power that differs from weapon to weapon: a handgun barely marks stone, a rocket puts a hole straight through it.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The Mining Drill Rig is here. Ride it, drive it where you want to dig, raise the mast, and bore. It clears a 5x5 face — 25 blocks at a time, against the handheld drill's 3x3 = 9.

The rig goes through obsidian. Its handling is deliberately poor in exchange: the auger will not turn until the mast is up, the machine cannot drive with the mast up, and it takes no input at all while the mast is moving.
Rig controls and a readout for the mast and the drill.
Every heavy item, projectile and ranged weapon can now damage blocks: eleven guns, the angel and royal arrows, the angel staff, and the siege maul.
The power differs by weapon. A handgun or SMG takes 50 shots to open stone, an assault rifle 19, a sniper 8, a heavy sniper 2, and a rocket launcher 1.
Hitting a block with the siege maul now breaks walls — stone in one swing, deepslate in two. It does not mine faster; it wears down a durability derived from hardness until the block gives.
An angel arrow opens stone in 38 hits, a royal arrow in a quarter of that. The angel staff's bolt burns through stone in 5.

sections.title: Balance changes
items: Anti-materiel damage per shot (durability is hardness x 100, so stone is 150 and obsidian 5000): handgun 3 / SMG 3 / minigun 4 / assault rifle 8 / shotgun 2 per pellet x10 / breaching shotgun 6 per pellet x10 / marksman carbine 12 / sniper 20 / heavy sniper 100 (unchanged) / laser 12 / rocket launcher 600 / angel arrow 4 / royal arrow 16 / angel staff 30 / siege maul 250.

sections.title: Warnings
items: The heavy sniper rifle is unchanged (stone in 2, obsidian in 50). V3.8.0 adds weapons that damage blocks; it does not re-balance the one that already did.

Guns can now damage builds, which changes how building works on survival and multiplayer servers. Land protection and permission checks still apply exactly as before. Setting a weapon's value to 0 in the config turns anti-materiel damage off for that weapon alone.
If you are already playing on a server, the new settings are written into your config file at startup. Without that, every gun would silently come out at 0 — no anti-materiel damage at all.
Unbreakable blocks such as bedrock cannot be damaged by any weapon.
The rig cannot move while drilling. Stow the mast to drive.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The rig clears far more per pass than the handheld drill, but takes longer per block.

The crack overlay is produced by different internals in the guns mod and the sky mod, because the mods hold no references to each other. The formula turning hardness into durability is identical in both.
There is no Minecraft client in the development environment, so the rig's appearance and the crack rendering have not been checked on real hardware.

groups.label: V3.7
groups.summary: The laser gun rebuilt as a real beam and tripled, the minigun's barrels spin, and the drill stops swinging

releases.title: The laser gun rebuilt as a real beam and tripled, the minigun's barrels spin, and the drill stops swinging
releases.summary: The laser gun was rebuilt: it now looks like the reference with an exposed glowing core, hits three times as hard (200 to 600), and fires a continuous beam while you hold the trigger instead of rapid discrete shots. The minigun's barrel cluster turns while it is actually firing. And the drill no longer plays a punch animation once every time you left-click.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The laser gun's shape was rebuilt: a white body, a dark muzzle housing, an exposed blue energy core with clamp rings, and a solid stock — much closer to the reference.
The laser gun hits three times as hard (200 to 600 per hit). If you are already playing on a server, the old value in your config file is updated automatically.
The laser gun is a beam weapon now, not a rapid-fire one. Hold the trigger and the beam stays on, damaging whatever it touches. Cell consumption is unchanged.
The minigun's barrels turn while rounds are actually leaving it. They stay still on an empty magazine, during spin-up and during the cooldown, and coast to a stop after the last round.
The drill no longer plays the punch animation that appeared once on every left-click.

sections.title: Warnings
items: The laser gun does 6,000 damage per second. That is the ordered 3x on each hit and nothing more — the beam still applies damage ten times a second, exactly as the old rapid fire did.
Because the drill's arm swing is suppressed, right-clicking to load a cell no longer swings your arm either. The loading sound and the charge readout are unchanged.
The minigun's barrel clamps went from square to octagonal so they do not read as a spinning nut when the cluster turns. They look slightly thicker.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The laser gun reads as changed, but it is not a close match to the reference. That gun's body is smoothly chamfered, which a model built from boxes cannot reach.
The minigun's octagonal clamps visibly facet as they turn — that is this pack's cylinder approximation showing.
This development environment has no Minecraft client, so neither the beam nor the spinning barrels have been seen in the actual game — only in offline renders.

groups.label: V3.6
groups.summary: Coloured glass lanterns now tint what they light, and only the drill's bit spins

releases.title: Coloured glass lanterns now tint what they light, and only the drill's bit spins
releases.summary: A coloured glass lantern now washes the floor and walls in its own colour — a red lantern makes the area red. The brightness is exactly as it was; only the colour changes. The drill no longer whirls as a whole tool: just the bit turns. It also mines every block at the same speed, fixing dirt, sand and gravel being drastically slow. And Corvus can now install and update Aureum, the lightweight optimisation mod, directly.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Coloured glass lanterns tint the floor and walls they light. A red lantern makes its surroundings red, a blue one blue. The light LEVEL is exactly as before — only the colour is new.
White, light gray, gray, black and the plain undyed lantern cast no colour, as before. That is decided automatically from how saturated the dye is, not from a hand-written list.
Only the drill's bit turns now. The whole tool used to spin on screen; the grip and housing now stay still and just the cutting head rotates.
The drill mines every block at the same speed. Dirt, sand and gravel used to be drastically slower, because vanilla did not consider the drill the right tool for them.
Its drops were fixed to match. A tool that digs fast but yields nothing would be worse than a slow one, so the drill now drops what it breaks — cobwebs give string, which they did not before.
Corvus can download and update Aureum, the lightweight optimisation mod, without opening the website.

sections.title: Warnings
items: Aureum is never installed automatically. It arrives only if you put it in your mods folder yourself or press Install in Corvus. Once it is there, new versions are picked up automatically, following your existing auto-update setting.

Because the drill is now uniform, cobwebs break instantly. Swords and shears already carry their own cobweb special case, so this is a change of degree rather than of kind — and cobwebs now drop string where they used to drop nothing.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The lantern colour is not real coloured light. Minecraft's engine cannot hold a colour per light source — block light is a single 0-15 number — so this lays a coloured film over the surfaces instead. Consequently colours do not add: a red and a blue lantern on the same floor do not make purple; whichever draws last wins.

For the same reason only block faces are tinted. Players, mobs and dropped items are not. Stairs, slabs, leaves, glass and water are not either, and thin shapes like fences cast no shadow in the wash.
A floor already lit by torches takes just as much colour as a dark one. Placing or breaking a lantern takes about half a second to show.
Green-family lanterns read very slightly brighter, because the eye weights green heavily. That is capped, at the cost of green looking olive rather than vivid lime.
Behaviour alongside shader mods (Iris/Sodium) has not been checked.
This development environment has no Minecraft client, so neither the lantern colour nor the drill's spin has ever been seen in the actual game — only in offline renders.

groups.label: V3.5
groups.summary: The wind turbine's blades now turn, and the drill's durability is 20x

releases.title: The wind turbine's blades now turn, and the drill's durability is 20x
releases.summary: The wind turbine's three blades actually rotate. The speed follows how much power it is making, so a turbine that is boxed in and generating nothing stands completely still — and 'blades turning, lamp off' tells you at a glance that the site is good but the cable is not connected. The blades are also smooth now, where they used to look stepped. The drill's durability is twenty times what it was (10240 to 204800).

sections.title: Highlights
items: The wind turbine's blades turn. At full output one revolution takes four seconds.
The speed follows the actual output. A turbine roofed in or buried, generating nothing, stands completely still; at low altitude it turns slowly. You can judge a site just by looking at it.
The blades are smooth now. Their diagonals used to look stepped; moving the rotor to a renderer means a blade can be built as one long tapered beam.
The drill's durability is twenty times what it was (10240 to 204800). If you are already playing on a server, the old value in your config file is updated to the new one automatically.

sections.title: Warnings
items: The blades sweep about 0.6 blocks wider than the space the turbine needs to be placed in. Turbines set exactly 11 blocks apart will appear to brush blades, so leave a little extra room.
The durability update rewrites the old value (10240) in your config file once. If you had set the drill's durability to something of your own, your value is respected and left alone.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: This development environment has no Minecraft client, so the blades have never been seen turning in the actual game — only in six offline frames rendered at different angles. The direction of rotation (clockwise seen from the front is what is intended) is likewise unconfirmed on a real client.
Whether light falls on the blades correctly at night is also unconfirmed in-game.

groups.label: V3.4
groups.summary: The wind turbine rebuilt as the reference's tubular machine, and nine guns rebuilt in SHAPE

releases.title: The wind turbine rebuilt as the reference's tubular machine, and nine guns rebuilt in SHAPE
releases.summary: The owner was right about V3.3.0's visual work: it was not enough. The reference shows a smooth tubular wind turbine, but what shipped was an open lattice mast — a different structural family — that had only been recoloured and made taller. The guns had only three of nine COLOURS changed and not one shape. Both are rebuilt here. The turbine is now a real tubular machine with a boxy nacelle, long tapered blades and a concrete base with stairs; the guns had their geometry matched to the reference, including the assault rifle's stock, the SMG's curved magazine and the shotgun's shell side-saddle.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The wind turbine is rebuilt. It goes from an open lattice mast to the reference's smooth tubular tower, with two red-and-white aviation bands on its upper half, a louvred nacelle with an anemometer, a rounded nose cone, three long tapered blades with red tips, and a concrete base with a handrail, an external staircase and an access door.
The rotor is now the right size. It spans about 12.5 blocks on a 16-block machine — the real machine's proportion. Before, the blades were a token roughly a tenth of the machine's height.

The assault rifle now has a properly shaped buttstock and a flip-up sight. The blue lens optic, which the reference does not have, is gone. Its overall proportions were stretched to match the reference too.
The submachine gun's stock is now a solid folding plate, and its magazine curves the way the real one does.
The shotgun gained the reference's most distinctive feature: a shell side-saddle, four red hulls over brass heads. The wooden shoulder stock, which the reference does not have, was removed.
The minigun's six bores are visible at last. A barrel clamp used to sit exactly level with the muzzle, so the whole muzzle face read as a gold disc.
The inventory icons were redrawn to match the rebuilt 3D models. The wooden stocks are gone from the assault rifle and shotgun icons, and the shotgun icon now shows its side-saddle.

sections.title: Warnings
items: This is an appearance-only release. Not one block, item or entity identifier changed, and no stats or hitboxes changed. Your world and configs carry over untouched.
The wind turbine needs a different amount of space to place (height 11 to 16 blocks, width 5 to 11). Because it is now hollow, however, the number of blocks it actually occupies fell from 200 to 133.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The blades' diagonals are visibly stepped. Rotated boxes cannot cross a block boundary in this rendering approach, so this is a limit rather than a defect to fix.
Faint horizontal seams appear every 8 pixels up the tower. At a distance they read as flange joints; close up the tower is chunkier than the reference.
The nacelle is blockier than the reference and slightly large relative to the hub. That is the 16-pixels-per-block resolution.
Among the guns, the shotgun and handgun read as the right KIND of weapon but are not close matches. Both reference guns have rounded, chamfered bodies that a model built from boxes cannot reach.
The assault rifle is now harder to pick out in a small inventory slot. Its orange wooden stock had been doing that work. Matching the 3D model was the requirement, and this is what it cost.
This development environment has no Minecraft client, so once again none of this has been seen in the actual game — only in offline renders.

groups.label: V3.3
groups.summary: A new phone mod, a much larger wind turbine, and tsunami water that finally drains

releases.title: A new phone mod, a much larger wind turbine, and tsunami water that finally drains
releases.summary: A twelfth mod, alpha-phone, is added: a smartphone you can carry, with Contacts, Messages and Settings (Do Not Disturb). Messages are stored server-side, so they survive a restart. The power mod's wind turbine grew from an 11-cell tower to a 20-cell one and gained the red-and-white aviation markings and red blade tips a real machine has. In the survival mod, water left behind by a tsunami now drains away instead of standing forever, and a tsunami now floods the inside of buildings — without breaking them.

sections.title: Highlights
items: NEW MOD: a smartphone. Hold it and right-click to open the screen, which carries Contacts, Messages and Settings. Messages travel between players on the same server and are stored server-side, so they survive a restart. Turning on Do Not Disturb in Settings stops new-message notifications.

The wind turbine is much bigger: its tower went from 11 cells to 20, tall enough to read from a distance. It also gained two red-and-white aviation warning bands on the tower and red blade tips, matching how a real turbine is painted.
Water from a tsunami now drains away. Until now, whatever flooded in simply stayed there.
A tsunami now floods the inside of buildings. Walls, doors and roofs are never broken — only the space inside fills with water.

The guns were brought closer to the reference art: the sniper rifle is olive so it is no longer hard to tell from the heavy sniper, the rocket launcher's tube is green, its lock-on sight is green, and the minigun gained a gold band.
Two vehicles were renamed and their trim recoloured (Coupe to Ferrari, Rally Car to Mercedes-AMG GT). No block or item identifier changed, so vehicles you already own keep working.
The MacBook Air and MacBook Pro now use a display-to-body thickness ratio closer to the real machines.

sections.title: Warnings
items: For now the phone can only be obtained from the creative-mode tab. There is no crafting recipe yet.
The phone mod is separate from the terminal that the decoration mod (alpha-deco) already ships. They share no code and no saved data, so having both installed changes nothing about either.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: This release follows 3.2.0. 3.1 is still skipped, and the features planned for V3.1 are not in yet.
The gun work changed the COLOURS of three of the nine weapons. No shapes were changed, so the other ten look exactly as they did before.
The wind turbine's item icon — the picture you see when holding it — is still the old one, with no bands and no lattice. Only the placed block looks new.
The phone mod does not yet have any of the automated checks the other mods carry. Its behaviour has been tested, but the machinery that would catch a future regression is still to be added.
This development environment has no Minecraft client, so none of this release's visual changes have been seen on a real screen yet. Please tell us if anything looks wrong.

groups.label: V3.2
groups.summary: Renamed to Corvus OS, the screen restyled as Linux, and the ATM rebuilt in three dimensions

releases.title: Renamed to Corvus OS, the screen restyled as Linux, and the ATM rebuilt in three dimensions
releases.summary: The computer and phone OS is renamed from Mine OS to Corvus OS, and the banking screen from Mine Bank to Corvus Bank — the same name the desktop app and this site already use. The OS is restyled to read as Linux, with a boot log, a calmer palette and a corvid mark. The computer's screen no longer shows the world through it: it is opaque now, like a real display. The ATM has been rebuilt so its slots and keypad are real shapes rather than pictures painted on a box.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Mine OS is now Corvus OS, and Mine Bank is now Corvus Bank. This is a display-name change only — not one block, item or config identifier has changed.
Corvus OS is restyled as Linux: a boot log of [ OK ] lines as it starts, a calmer charcoal palette, and a corvid mark in place of the old cube.
The computer's screen is no longer see-through. The world behind it used to show through the display; it is now opaque and reads as a real screen. The phone keeps its frosted glass.
Maximising a window now hides the Dock and gives the window that space for real; restoring brings it back. The phone's home bar is unchanged.

The ATM has been rebuilt in three dimensions. The blue sign, the light strip beneath it, the recessed screen, the card, receipt and cash slots, the keypad shelf, the corner pillars and the plinth are all real geometry now instead of a painted box. The Special ATM gets the same shape in its gold livery.

sections.title: Warnings
items: The rename is cosmetic. No block, item or config identifier changed, so existing worlds and settings files carry on working exactly as before.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: This release follows 3.0.0. There is no 3.1 — the features planned in V3.1 are not in yet.
The visual changes have not been checked on a real screen, because there is no Minecraft client in the development environment. Please report anything that looks wrong.
The new mark loses its finer detail below about 16 px. That limit is known and accepted.

groups.label: V3.0
groups.summary: V3, part one: three storage blocks, a rebuilt drone, and the Meridian Store

releases.title: V3, part one: three storage blocks, a rebuilt drone, and the Meridian Store
releases.summary: This release brings the first five of the features planned for V3. Three new storage blocks — the Silt Filter Pump, which lifts items out of water; the Grain Silo, which holds a great deal of one item; and the Glass Amphora, which stores a fluid and shows the level through the glass — arrive alongside a drone rebuilt from scratch, now with first-person piloting, warhead drops and chest carrying. There is also the Meridian Store, an in-game shop that flies your order to you by drone. Payment uses the emeralds you already have (or your MineBank account); no new currency is introduced.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added the Silt Filter Pump. Every 10 ticks it searches the water in front of it, lifts out any dropped items and stores them internally (5 stacks). Put samples in its 5 filter slots and it collects only those kinds. It will not pull items through solid blocks, and a hopper can draw from underneath.

Added the Grain Silo. It locks to the first item kind put in and holds up to 128 stacks of it (8,192 wheat). A comparator reads the amount, hoppers move items in and out, and the kind can only be reset while the silo is empty.

Added the Glass Amphora. It holds 8 buckets of a single fluid with the level visible from outside. Fill or empty it with a bucket, read the amount with a comparator, and note that fluids cannot be mixed — empty it first. Breaking it with Silk Touch keeps the contents.

The drone has been rebuilt from the ground up: a new model, first-person piloting, warhead carriage and drops, and picking up and carrying chests. Piloting does not capture your mouse — the drone is steered relative to the centre of the screen, with a dead zone in the middle. A large chest is too much for a single drone.

Added the Meridian Store. Order from an in-game terminal and a delivery drone flies from the depot to drop your parcel at your beacon. Pay with the emeralds in your inventory or from your MineBank account; refunds return by whichever route you paid.

sections.title: Warnings
items: Drone warhead drops only work if a firearms module is installed on the server. Without one the drone says so plainly and nothing happens.
Drone piloting, warheads and chest carriage can each be disabled independently in the server settings.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: This release contains five of the fifty features planned for V3 (#21, #22, #29, #38, and the first phase of #50). The rest will follow in later releases — this is not the complete V3.
The look and feel of everything added here has not yet been checked on a real screen, because there is no Minecraft client in the development environment. Please report anything that looks wrong.
The drone deliberately does not capture the mouse. In Minecraft 26.2 there is no way to recover a stuck mouse grab short of logging back in, so that risk is avoided by design.

groups.label: V2.5
groups.summary: A lighter tactical map for the missile launcher, plus the data behind Corvus's new Solo Play Tuning screen

releases.title: A lighter tactical map for the missile launcher, plus the data behind Corvus's new Solo Play Tuning screen
releases.summary: The missile launcher's tactical map used to bog down while you were picking targets (dragging and zooming); that is now much lighter. Alongside it, server administrators get a /packintegrity command for checking what is installed, and this release adds the data that the new "Solo Play Tuning" screen in the Corvus desktop app needs in order to work in single-player.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Made the missile launcher's tactical map much lighter while you are picking targets with terrain drawn. Nothing about how it looks or how it is operated has changed.

Added a /packintegrity command for server administrators, which checks that the full set of mods is present and correct (the result is also written to logs/pack_integrity.log). It has no effect on play.

Added, from this release, the data that lets the new "Solo Play Tuning" screen in the Corvus desktop app (Settings → Solo Play Tuning) adjust the same items as the admin settings directly in single-player. Update Corvus to the latest version to use it.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The "Solo Play Tuning" screen requires Corvus 1.7.0 or newer. It does not appear in earlier versions of Corvus.

releases.title: Seven previously undocumented mechanics, written up on the Feature Guide page
releases.summary: V2.5.1 already ships with seven mechanics, all on by default, that have never had a changelog write-up: weather systems, the price multiplier, the diamond ATM balance, retroactive nuclear-plant pollution, dehydration death, vehicle gasoline, and mask durability. We checked each one directly against the shipped mod code and wrote it up on the Feature Guide page. Nothing about any mechanic or its defaults changed to produce this entry.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Weather systems (blizzard, typhoon, earthquake, tsunami, volcano) — all five on by default. Earthquakes can break structures built from stone, cobblestone, dirt, sand, or gravel even with the default settings; volcanoes erupt on a 5% chance per earthquake, carving a real 6-block-radius, 4-block-deep crater and filling it with lava (built structures usually stop this outright — see the Feature Guide for how).

The price multiplier (×10–×100) is on by default in Sky and Planarcadia (not vanilla villager trades). The same code is also copied into Guns, Rail, Power, and Backrooms, but nothing there currently reads it.
The diamond ATM balance is on by default in Building & Decor — a second balance alongside emeralds, at a fixed 1 diamond = 4 emerald rate.
Nuclear-plant air pollution is on by default and retroactive. (The mechanic itself was mentioned in V2.0.0; the retroactivity and the default weren't stated until now.)
Dehydration death: staying at 0 hydration for 10 minutes straight starts damage that can now actually kill you on any difficulty except Peaceful.

Vehicle gasoline is on by default, can be turned off in config, and existing vehicles carry over with a full tank. (Gasoline itself was announced in V2.0.0; the toggle and the legacy-vehicle handling weren't.)
Masks (Sparkle/Sparxie) have 814 durability and revive once, 320 seconds after breaking.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: This entry changes no mechanic and no default. It documents seven things that were already running, after checking each directly against the shipped mod code. Full detail and the exact config key for each is on the Feature Guide page.
We didn't trace exactly which version first introduced the price multiplier or the diamond balance — only that both are confirmed live as of V2.5.1.

releases.title: [Please read first] Delete the old glimpse-alpha-*.jar files before installing — the mods are now called "Alpha", not "Glimpse Alpha"
releases.summary: ⚠ Before you install this release, delete all 11 jars beginning with "glimpse-alpha-" from your mods folder. If you do not, neither Minecraft nor the server will start. The mods have been renamed from "Glimpse Alpha" to "Alpha" (the owner asked for "Glimpse" to be dropped), so the jar filenames change from "glimpse-alpha-something.jar" to "alpha-something.jar". Only the name is different — the game treats them as the same mods, so leaving the old ones in place means "the same mod is installed twice" and Fabric stops the launch right there (the error reads Duplicate mod). Delete only the 11 files that begin with "glimpse-alpha-" — do not delete the jar starting with "fabric-api", or any other mod you installed yourself. Nothing but the name has changed. Not one character of the internal block and item IDs was touched, so the buildings you have already put up, the tools you are carrying, your world and your config all keep working exactly as before. If you use the Corvus launcher, the app removes the old jars for you and you do not need to do any of this.

sections.title: Highlights
items: [The one thing to do first] Open your mods folder and delete all 11 jars beginning with "glimpse-alpha-", then add the 11 new ones beginning with "alpha-". Adding the new ones without deleting the old ones stops both Minecraft and the server from starting. Deleting first, before you add anything, is the safest order.

Delete only the files that begin with "glimpse-alpha-". "fabric-api-….jar" is required for Alpha to run at all, so never delete that one. Any other mods you installed yourself are fine where they are.
If you do forget and it will not start, your world is not damaged. Remove the jars beginning with "glimpse-alpha-" from the mods folder and it will start as normal.
The mods have been renamed from "Glimpse Alpha" to "Alpha". "Glimpse" disappears from the in-game creative tab names, the key-binding category name, and the name shown in the mod list.
Jar filenames are now "alpha-something-2.5.0+mc26.2.jar", and the distributed ZIP is now named "Alpha_MODs_v2.5.0+mc26.2.zip".

Not one character of the internal block, item and entity IDs (all 11 of them: sorakaze_guns and the rest) has changed. Blocks you have already placed and items you are holding will not disappear, and there is no need to start a new world.
The config filenames also stay as "config/sorakaze_*.json". Any values you tuned yourself carry straight over.
The server admin commands (/glimpsebackup, /glimpse storm restore) keep the names they had. Changing something already wired into scripts and habits is a change of behaviour, not a change of name.
If you use Corvus launcher 1.5.1, the app deletes the old jars for you. Anyone putting files into the mods folder by hand, and server administrators, should delete them themselves as described above.

sections.title: Warnings
items: Before installing this release, delete all 11 jars beginning with "glimpse-alpha-" from your mods folder. Forget, and the same mods are present twice, and neither Minecraft nor the server will start.
Do not delete the jar beginning with "fabric-api". Alpha needs that file to run.
If you run a server, the same deletion has to be done in the server's own mods folder as well.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: Corvus launcher 1.5.1 still shows the previous name ("Glimpse Alpha") on screen. It is a display issue only and does not affect update checking, downloading or installing. In the next launcher update the display name will be read from the release feed and this will resolve itself.

The page descriptions across this Wiki have already been switched to "Alpha" in all 13 languages. Past changelog entries, however, still read "Glimpse Alpha" as they were written — that genuinely was the name at the time, so they stand as a record.

The in-game command names (/glimpsebackup, /glimpse storm restore) and the admin audit file (glimpse-admin/audit.log) keep "glimpse" in them. Renaming a command would break existing scripts, and renaming the log file would make the history already in it unreadable, so both were deliberately left alone.
"Glimpse Glass", the name of the visual design language, is not a mod name and stays as it is.

groups.label: V2.4
groups.summary: Fixed the missile launcher rendering as two models at once, map panning moved to right-drag, 100 targets per salvo and a 200-round magazine you open like a chest. Also fixes a Backrooms server crash

releases.title: Fixed the missile launcher rendering as two models at once, map panning moved to right-drag, 100 targets per salvo and a 200-round magazine you open like a chest. Also fixes a Backrooms server crash
releases.summary: This release answers four points the owner raised about the missile launcher. The model that had ended up as "the old design fused with the new one" is fixed, the tactical map no longer moves when you merely click it, the number of targets you can aim at in one go is now 100, and the magazine has been rebuilt as a 200-round storage container. Alongside that, a bug that could force the server to shut down when it loaded a Backrooms Level 0 chunk generated before V2.4.x has been fixed. That one never happens in a freshly created world, which is why it had gone unnoticed until now. If your server has a world people have already been playing in, this is the most important change here.

sections.title: Highlights
items: [Server crash fixed] Fixed a bug where loading a Backrooms Level 0 chunk generated before V2.4.x could make the server stop responding and force-quit about 60 seconds later. The pass that redraws old chunks to the new look now runs after the chunk has loaded rather than during the load. It never happens in a freshly created world, which is why our testing never caught it. Only worlds that have been played in for a while are affected.

Fixed the missile launcher's model appearing as "the old design fused with the new one". There were two causes: (1) the legs and missile tube were drawn 180 degrees out in all four facings, so the missile tube sat one block in front of the pad and two of the four legs were drawn hanging in the air, and (2) 7 of the old design's 13 block models were still being drawn alongside the new ones. Both are fixed, and apart from the ground pad only the new geometry is now drawn.

While fixing that, it emerged that since V2.4.6 the launch pad's leg collision boxes had been wrong in three of the four facings (this had not been reported). They have been rebuilt to be correct per facing.

Panning the tactical map moved from press-and-hold left-click to press-and-hold right-click. Left-click now only adds and removes targets, so the map no longer moves when you simply click it. A pan does not begin until the pointer has travelled at least 3 pixels from where it was pressed (previously tiny hand tremors accumulated and the view drifted while you believed it was still). The controls are also shown along the bottom of the map screen.

The number of targets markable on the tactical map was raised from 50 to 100. So that a bigger salvo does not cost more performance, the in-flight trail effect and the impact processing now have a per-tick budget and are worked through in order. Impacts over that budget are carried to the next tick rather than discarded, so no round you fired ever vanishes.

The magazine was raised from 50 to 200 rounds and rebuilt as a chest-shaped storage screen (6 rows × 9 columns). Open it by crouching and right-clicking (a plain right-click still opens the control panel as before). The control panel has also gained a "Magazine" button. Holding a warhead and right-clicking still loads it one at a time on the spot, as before.

A hopper attached to any block of the launch pad (all 36 cells of its 3×4×3 volume) will restock the magazine. Missile warheads and nuclear warheads can be left mixed together, and can be reordered however you like in the storage screen.
Anything loaded in the magazine before V2.4.9 is carried straight over into the new format when the world loads. No rounds are lost.

sections.title: Balance changes
items: Missile launcher magazine capacity: 50 rounds → 200 rounds. Maximum targets markable on the map: 50 → 100.

sections.title: Warnings
items: The tactical map's controls have changed. Panning the view is now press-and-hold RIGHT-click. Press-and-hold left-click no longer pans (left-click is exclusively for adding and removing targets).
A hopper can restock the magazine, but deliberately cannot pull items back out of it. That is to stop a magazine you have just filled being quietly drained by a hopper attached to it.

There is nothing to delete or edit in your config. The new defaults for magazine size and target count (200 rounds, 100 targets) are applied automatically at startup, and any values you changed yourself are left as they are.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: "100 at once" is a design ceiling set alongside a per-tick processing budget. It is not a figure measured by actually putting 100 rounds in the air at the same time.
The teal glow lines on the legs and missile tube are a static, always-lit part of the paintwork, not a firing/standby indicator that switches on and off (this limitation carries over from V2.4.6).
Right-dragging the tactical map translates the view only. There is no rotation and no 3D tilt.

releases.title: Genuinely splayed, tapering legs and missile tube; a higher-resolution tactical map you can drag; magazine and targets raised to 50
releases.summary: The missile launcher's legs and missile tube have gone from stacked cuboids to purpose-drawn geometry that really does splay and taper, using the same every-frame direct rendering as the turret's rotating head. The tactical map's terrain resolution has been raised sharply, and alongside mouse-wheel zoom you can now hold left-click and drag to fine-tune the view. The magazine and the target list have both been raised from 10 to 50, and the Wiki has gained the steps for setting the admin app's own ID and password.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The missile launcher's legs have gone from stacked cuboids to legs that genuinely taper inwards from their outer footing towards the centre, with a joint. The missile tube is likewise no longer a cuboid but a genuinely tapering octagonal barrel with a tip. Both are drawn with the same every-frame direct rendering as the automatic turret's rotating head, and the collision box is unchanged.
Teal glow lines were added to the legs and the missile tube.
The tactical map's terrain rendering went from one sample per 4 screen pixels to one sample per screen pixel — four times the resolution in practice.
Holding left-click and moving on the tactical map now fine-tunes the view (separate from the zoom's cursor-following, so you can put the spot you are aiming at anywhere on the screen you like).
The missile launcher's magazine was raised from 30 to 50 rounds, and the number of targets you can mark on the map from 10 to 50 — after burst-firing tests with 10 rounds came back clean.
The Wiki's install guide gained the steps for the owner to set the in-game admin app's own ID and password (the actual credentials are not published — knowing the steps does not let you sign in).

sections.title: Balance changes
items: Missile launcher magazine capacity: 30 rounds → 50 rounds. Maximum targets markable on the map: 10 → 50.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The teal LED lines on the legs and missile tube are a static, always-lit part of the paintwork, not a firing/standby indicator that switches on and off (this limitation carries over from V2.4.6).
Dragging the tactical map translates the view only. There is no rotation and no 3D tilt.

releases.title: Missile launcher reworked: a 30-round mixed magazine, 10-target burst fire, a rebuilt launch pad, and louder impacts
releases.summary: Going back over the owner's reference design, the missile launcher's launch pad has been rebuilt rather than merely recoloured: it now has four legs that genuinely splay outwards and a tablet screen on its flank showing the tactical map. The magazine has been enlarged to 30 rounds — missiles and nuclear warheads can be loaded side by side — and up to 10 targets can be marked on the tactical map and fired at in one continuous burst, like a burst rifle. Impact sounds for both missile and nuclear warheads now carry further and hit harder.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The launch pad has been rebuilt: four legs at the corners that genuinely read as splaying outwards (a stepped silhouette, broad where it meets the ground and tapering upwards), plus a tablet screen on the flank showing the tactical map in the same colours as the real map screen.
The magazine now holds up to 30 rounds. Missile warheads and nuclear warheads can be mixed in the same magazine, and are fired in the order they were loaded.
Up to 10 targets can now be marked on the tactical map. Each click on the map adds a target there and then — there is no separate "confirm" step — and clicking an existing pin removes it.
Pressing fire sends one round at a time towards the marked targets in a continuous burst, like a burst rifle: the next round launches as each target is consumed from the queue.
Missile warhead impacts now also carry on a wide broadcast (up to 6,000 blocks). Previously they could only be heard from very close by.
Impact sounds for both nuclear and missile warheads have more low end, and are louder on both the close-range and wide broadcasts.

sections.title: Balance changes
items: Missile launcher magazine capacity: 4 rounds → 30 rounds (mixed loading).

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The launch pad's teal LED lines are a static, always-lit part of the paintwork, not a firing/standby indicator that switches on and off (this limitation carries over from V2.4.6).

The four corner legs are not truly angled geometry: three stacked axis-aligned boxes form a stepped silhouette that approximates a splayed leg. That is a deliberate design rule for this whole set — it avoids adding rotated collision maths.

releases.title: Real terrain and zoom on the missile launcher's tactical map, and a redesigned launch pad
releases.summary: The tactical map added in V2.4.5 drew coordinates and symbols but nothing you could recognise as a place, and at the scale needed to show a 2,000-block range, short-range aiming was so coarse that shots landed somewhere you never intended. The map now draws real terrain colours using the same mechanism as the vanilla map item, and the mouse wheel zooms in and out around the cursor. The launch pad's own 3D model — deliberately left alone in the previous update — has also been reworked along the owner's reference design, into an olive-drab and dark-steel palette with leg-like struts at the four corners and teal glow lines picked out across it.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The tactical map now draws real terrain: it uses the same surface-block colours as the vanilla map item, with simple shading derived from the height difference to the neighbouring sample. Only areas already loaded on your own client are drawn (anything not loaded stays the same neutral "unknown" colour as before).

Added mouse-wheel zoom in and out. Zooming is centred on the cursor, so you can move in on the spot you care about without first dragging it to the middle of the screen. A "Back to launcher" button returns you to the original scale and centre.
The launch pad's 3D model has been reworked: an olive-drab and dark-steel palette, leg-like struts at the four corners, and teal glow lines on the body, the struts and the missile tube.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The launch pad's teal LED lines are a static, always-lit part of the paintwork. They do not switch on and off to reflect a firing or standby state.
Terrain is re-sampled whenever the view moves (a zoom, or "Back to launcher"), not every frame. On a very low-powered machine a coarse image can persist for a moment after you zoom in.
The map cannot be panned by dragging. The view only moves by following the cursor while zooming, or by the "Back to launcher" button.

releases.title: Missile launcher targeting redesigned: click a tactical map instead of typing coordinates
releases.summary: Missile launcher targeting has been redesigned from typed coordinates to a point-and-click tactical map. The map shows a range ring (2,000 blocks by default), and the selected point is colour-coded to show at a glance whether it's in range. The actual impact height is now determined automatically from the real ground surface at the selected point, computed by the server. Selecting an area that hasn't been loaded yet fails with a clear message instead of failing silently. Range checking now uses horizontal distance only, so terrain height differences can no longer make the map's range ring disagree with what the launcher will actually accept. Existing safety, firing, warhead, and cooldown systems are unchanged. The launcher's in-world 3D model has not been changed in this update.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Added an "Open Map" button to the missile launcher's control panel; the typed-coordinate fields have been removed.

Tactical map: shows the launcher centred, a range ring (2,000 blocks by default), your own position, and the selected pin. The pin is colour-coded (in range / out of range) with the distance shown as text.

Confirming sends only the selected XZ point to the server, which determines the real impact height from the ground surface itself. Confirming a point in an area that isn't loaded shows a clear "area not loaded" message and leaves the existing target unchanged.
Range checking changed from full 3D distance to horizontal distance only, so terrain height differences can no longer make the map's range ring and the actual firing gate disagree.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The launcher's in-world 3D model (its appearance) has not been changed in this update - it keeps its existing look.
The map does not support zooming or panning yet - it always shows a fixed-scale view centred on the launcher.

The ground-height preview under the pin only works for areas already loaded on your own client, which is most of the time outside view distance for a 2,000-block range - it will usually show "unknown until confirmed" (the server always computes the real height correctly once you confirm).

releases.title: Admin app login consolidated to a single shared credential; fixed operator permissions being wiped
releases.summary: Reports of "I enter the admin ID and password and still can't log in" persisted, so the owner decided to redesign the admin app's sign-in model itself. It no longer binds 3 separate accounts to 3 specific Minecraft names - there is now a single shared ID and password, and anyone who knows both can sign in from any Minecraft account. While investigating, a serious separate bug was found: when the admin account file is missing or broken, the server would automatically strip real operator (/op) permission from every player who had it - introduced in V2.4.0, this had been silently blocking command usage and things like the auto-backup toggle. That is also fixed in this release.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Admin app sign-in changed from 3 name-locked accounts to a single shared ID and password. Anyone who knows both can sign in, regardless of which Minecraft account they're connected as.

Fixed a serious bug where the automatic server-operator (/op) sync would strip operator permission from every existing operator whenever the admin account file was missing or broken. It now leaves existing operator status untouched until the file is properly configured.
For server owners: updated the credential-recovery steps for the new single-account model (private documentation).

sections.title: Warnings
items: Admin app access is now a single shared credential rather than per-person. To revoke access from one specific person without affecting everyone else is no longer possible with this design - rotate the shared password instead and redistribute it only to who should keep access.

releases.title: Server Admin login now distinguishes the real cause, plus 3 known issues fixed
releases.summary: A fix release for reports of "I enter the admin ID and password and still can't log in." No defect was found in the network path or the credential-verification logic itself, but the sign-in screen previously showed the exact same "wrong ID or password" message whether the server simply had zero admin accounts configured yet, or the entered credentials were genuinely wrong - there was no way to tell which. It now shows a distinct message for the former case, and login attempts made in that state no longer count against the anti-brute-force limiter. Also fixes 3 items that had been sitting on the Wiki's Known Issues page: reinforced glass window colour names, a cable glow bug right after a power off/on toggle, and the "Lookup" app's recipe grid layout.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Server Admin app sign-in screen: when the server has zero valid admin accounts configured, it now shows a clear message saying so instead of the generic "wrong ID or password". Login attempts made in this state are no longer counted toward the anti-brute-force lockout.
Fixed the reinforced glass window (17 colours) display names - every colour now shows its proper Japanese/English name.
Fixed cables that were disconnected from a breaker panel sometimes staying lit right after switching the main breaker off and back on.
Fixed the "Lookup" app's 3x3 recipe grid to show ingredients in their real crafting-grid positions (including empty cells), instead of packing them in order from the top-left.
For server owners: clarified the check/recovery steps for when a missing or malformed admin_account.json turns out to be the actual login cause (private owner-facing documentation).

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The admin login fix addresses the "zero accounts configured" case specifically. If all 3 accounts are correctly configured but one specific account still can't sign in, that is a different symptom - please report it separately.

The orphaned-cable fix takes full effect from an update correctly applied on this version onward. If you jump straight from V2.4.2 or earlier, one already-orphaned cable may still show live once; breaking and replacing it, or the next breaker toggle, clears it.

releases.title: Fixed a client crash when deploying a drone, and the Server Admin app's sign-in screen
releases.summary: A player-reported fix release. Deploying a drone previously crashed the client every time; it now works and renders a small quadcopter model. The Server Admin app's sign-in screen also no longer clears the ID field after every failed login attempt.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Fixed a client crash that happened every time a drone was deployed. Drones now render a small quadcopter model instead of crashing the client.
Fixed the Server Admin app's sign-in screen resetting the ID field to empty after every failed login attempt, which made retyping it necessary each time.

releases.title: Glass lanterns properly fixed, sanity no longer shares the screen with thirst, turret weapons are visible, and Glimpse Launcher arrives
releases.summary: The V2.2.1 glass lantern fix turned out not to be enough — a player sent a real screenshot showing the lanterns still reading as washed-out and near-white. We've redesigned them properly this time, removing the leftover white-hot centre entirely in favour of a single smooth colour gradient. In the Backrooms, the ordinary thirst bar was still showing up alongside sanity; it's now correctly hidden there. Weapons mounted on turrets were invisible even though they worked correctly; they now render. Several admin settings commands that were documented but didn't actually do anything have been wired up properly. And we're releasing a new desktop app, Glimpse Launcher, that checks for and applies pack updates automatically.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Redesigned the glass lantern glow again. V2.2.1's fix kept a small white-hot "filament" at the centre of each lantern, but in real play that filament still read as washed-out white regardless of colour — confirmed with a real in-game screenshot. The filament concept has been removed entirely in favour of a single smooth gradient from the centre to the edge. Still genuinely translucent glass.
Fixed the ordinary thirst bar showing up alongside sanity while inside the Backrooms. It's now correctly hidden there (the feature itself is unaffected everywhere else).
Fixed weapons mounted on turrets being invisible. Turrets have always accepted, fired, and returned mounted weapons correctly — they just never rendered. They now do.

Fixed several server admin settings commands that were documented but had no effect (village raid chance and wave count, video resolution cap, and others). The Backrooms module also gained its own admin settings entry point, which it previously had none of.

Released Glimpse Launcher, a new desktop app that checks the Wiki for pack updates, verifies downloads by SHA-256, takes an automatic backup before applying an update, and can open the official Minecraft Launcher for you (you still choose the Fabric profile yourself, exactly as before). One file runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux (Java is required to run it). Get it from the Download page.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: This is Glimpse Launcher's first release. The launcher cannot yet update itself automatically — that's planned for a future version.

groups.label: V2.2
groups.summary: Glass lanterns now genuinely glow in colour, and the Backrooms Level 1 crate mission is fixed

releases.title: Glass lanterns now genuinely glow in colour, and the Backrooms Level 1 crate mission is fixed
releases.summary: A player-reported fix release. Glass lanterns had a washed-out, near-white glow that barely showed their colour; they now read as translucent coloured glass genuinely glowing in their own hue, like neon. The Backrooms Level 1 "open 4 crates" objective, which could never be completed, has also been fixed.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Fixed glass lanterns' appearance: previously the colour was almost entirely washed out by a large white-hot core, so every lantern looked much the same near-white regardless of colour. Now the coloured glow dominates the block, neon-style — red lanterns glow red, blue glow blue, and so on — with only a small white-hot filament left at the very centre. As proper glass, you can still see through it.

Fixed the Backrooms Level 1 "open 4 crates" objective, which never progressed no matter how many crates you opened. Prying a crate open (with a crowbar, or crouch + bare hands) now correctly advances the objective.

releases.title: 52 new glass lanterns, a real Backrooms lobby, overworld raids, turrets, and a real reconstruction of Sapporo
releases.summary: This round adds an 11th mod, Sapporo — a dimension recreating the real city of Sapporo, Japan, from real survey data. Backrooms Level 1, "The Lobby", is now a real explorable space rather than a demo room, with a glass objective panel shown on the left of the screen at all times. Village raids can now trigger on pure chance without Bad Omen, turrets let you mount guns and bows, video now plays up to 4K and stops automatically when you walk away, the Sparxie staff gained a ranged attack alongside its melee one, the minigun and rocket launcher were rebalanced, a flyable camera drone and its own phone app arrived, and the Building & Decor mod gained 52 new glass lanterns. The Amethyst Gate now opens with plain vanilla amethyst blocks too.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The Sapporo mod (sorakaze_sapporo) has finally shipped. It's a dimension recreating the real city of Sapporo, Japan, from real geographic data. Building footprints and terrain are both 100% real survey data, but most building heights are currently a documented per-district statistical estimate — an honest gap while the more detailed 3D building dataset (Japan's PLATEAU) is still being obtained. Heights will be refined once that data is in hand.
Backrooms Level 1, "The Lobby", is now a real, walkable, explorable space rather than a small demo room. You reach it through a rift that generates naturally near an End City.
A glass objective panel is now shown on the left side of the screen at all times, showing your current level, sanity, and where to head next.

Inside the Backrooms, sanity now replaces thirst as the stat you're managing. Entities you meet there take no damage from ordinary weapons and cannot be defeated — this is a place for evasion, not combat.
The Amethyst Gate can now be built from plain vanilla amethyst blocks as well as Portal Amethyst Blocks — the two can even be mixed in the same frame.
Village raids can now start on pure chance just from being in a village, with no need for Bad Omen. 12 waves in total, with extra enemies from the Heaven mod on the final wave.
New turrets let you mount a gun, bow, or crossbow. A mounted weapon carries its own ammo store, and unmounting hands the weapon and remaining ammo back to you.
Video playback now supports up to 4K, always keeps a 16:9 aspect ratio, and stops automatically once you walk far enough away from the screen.
The Sparxie staff can now attack at range (a 24-block bolt) as well as in melee.
The minigun now hits roughly three times as hard, and the rocket launcher's blast is far more powerful than before.

A freely flyable camera drone was added, along with a dedicated Drone App on the in-game phone showing a live 16:9 feed from its point of view. Letting go leaves it hovering in place rather than auto-returning.
The Building & Decor mod gained 52 new glass lanterns (18 vanilla-glass, 17 reinforced, 17 blackout). Full light level 15, and measured brighter than the existing LED panel.
The admin app's PC screen gained a change-log view for the server administrator — a read-only view of past changes. Viewing it is not itself logged.

sections.title: Balance changes
items: Minigun damage roughly tripled.
Rocket launcher blast power greatly increased.

sections.title: Warnings
items: Playing in the Sapporo dimension requires the server administrator to have installed a separate map data file on the server (not distributed on this site). Without it, that world simply isn't reachable.
Backrooms entities cannot be defeated. Don't try to fight them with ordinary weapons — evade instead.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: Most Sapporo building heights are still a district-level statistical estimate rather than real survey data. They'll be updated once more detailed 3D city data becomes available.
Whether players can build and light their own Heaven gate (glowstone portal) depends on a server-administrator setting, which defaults to off.

releases.title: Backrooms Levels 3–8 become real, endless levels; a server-admin app on the in-game PC; boss summon recipes reach the recipe book
releases.summary: The largest change this round is Backrooms Levels 3 through 8. They used to be 128-block demo islands; they are now endless levels you can actually walk into and explore. The in-game PC in the Building & Decor mod gained a server-administration app, and in the Boss mod the summoning items' recipes now appear in the in-game recipe book. The three data-driven guns each have their own in-hand model at last.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Only four mods actually changed: Backrooms, Building & Decor, Boss and Guns. The other six (Planarcadia, Power, Rail, Sky, Survival, Vehicles) were bumped to 2.1.0 only to keep the set consistent — their jars differ from the 2.0.0 ones in exactly one entry, the version string in fabric.mod.json. Not a byte of their content changed.
Backrooms Levels 3 to 8 went from 128-block demo islands to real, endless levels. None of them has an edge any more; all of them can be walked and explored.
Level 3, the Electrical Station. The current is live and touching a panel is dangerous. A Hound patrols, and a Smiler waits in the underground cable room.
Level 4, the Empty Offices. Rated safe — but 3% of the windows are watching you, and they look exactly like the rest. Sanity slowly recovers here. The almond water is in the break room.
Level 5, the Terror Hotel. 80% of the numbered doors are locked. In each contiguous region exactly one room differs in its details. Do not linger.

Level 6, Lights Out. A flashlight works properly for 20 seconds; past that it only works about 15% of any given second. While it is lit, entities notice you from four times as far — light attracts. This is a level you navigate by ear.
Level 7, Thalassophobia. One house of fixed shape, and an ocean with no far shore. Do not walk to the end of the pier.
Level 8, the Cave System. Tunnels dug for people and then abandoned; the iron rails really do lead somewhere. There is a flooded winze 32 blocks deep.

The in-game PC gained a "Server Admin" app. Without opening a config file, an administrator can change: whether phone messaging, calls and the browser are allowed; how many camera feeds can be shown at once and whether live feeds are allowed; whether automatic backups run, how often, and how many are kept; and a set of boss knobs (Plague Doctor natural spawn and its chance, thunderstorm-only spawning, respawn cooldown, Plague Wither pack size, wardens required for the Sculk Golem, the Reaper's wither summon count, whether Rock Lock spawners generate in nether fortresses, Plague Doctor max health, Plague Wither health multiplier).

Opening the admin app needs an admin ID and a password. The server administrator hands those out individually, only to the people they choose. They are not written anywhere on this site. Sign-in expires after a while, and failed attempts are rate-limited.

The recipes for the Boss mod's summoning items (Forge Altar Core, Molten Crown, Sculk Heart, Sonar Eye, Frost Altar, Primal Egg, Soul Blood Altar) now appear in the in-game recipe book. Until now they had no unlock path at all, so there was no way to discover how to make them from inside the game.
Four discovery advancements were added as a hint toward summoning: The Scorching Key, The Fathom Key, The Frost Key and The Altar Is Built. Each fires when you hold the matching summoning item.
The Plague Doctor's natural spawn is available again, behind an administrator toggle — but it defaults to OFF. Until an administrator explicitly turns it on, behaviour is identical to V2.0.0.

The three data-driven guns (Service Pistol, Marksman Carbine, Breaching Shotgun) each have their own in-hand model now. All three had been borrowing the assault rifle's mesh, so holding a pistol showed you a rifle.

sections.title: Warnings
items: Levels 3 to 8 generate in a fundamentally different way now. In a world where you visited the demo islands under V2.0.0, the terrain in that area will not match what was there before.
The admin ID and password for the Server Admin app are never published on this site. Get them from the server administrator directly.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
items: The Sapporo mod (sorakaze_sapporo) is not part of this round. It is deferred to V2.2.
The actual look, sound and entity behaviour of Levels 3–8 had not been confirmed in a real play-through at the time of writing.

releases.title: The V2 update — a 10th mod, Planarcadia; four new bosses; plumbing, gasoline and food spoilage
releases.summary: This is V2 proper. The 10th mod, Planarcadia, shipped here for the first time. The Boss mod gained four new bosses, each with its own summoning ritual; Survival gained water infrastructure and a refrigerator; Vehicles gained gasoline; Power gained an air purifier. The Backrooms grew a great deal, and Building & Decor gained blackout reinforced glass in every colour.

sections.title: Highlights
items: A 10th mod, Planarcadia (sorakaze_planarcadia), is bundled for the first time. Build a frame out of Portal Amethyst Blocks in the same shape as a Nether portal, light it, and it opens onto a pleasure world where night rules. It brings its own blocks — LED signs, the phantom moon, the Interplanar Jump Mural, a shop counter. It does not depend on any other Glimpse Alpha mod.

Four new bosses joined the Boss mod: the Volcanic Golem King (Forge Altar Core + Molten Crown), the Abyssal Kraken Warden (Sculk Heart + Sonar Eye), the Prismatic Ice Phoenix Dragon (Frost Altar + Primal Egg), and the Witherstorm Demon Overlord (Soul Blood Altar + 3 wither skeleton skulls + a nether star).

The Soul Blood Altar refuses the Witherstorm Demon Overlord until all three of the others have been killed. Each of the four has a guaranteed drop: the Volcanic Core, the Abyssal Sinew, the Prismatic Plume and the Overlord's Heart.
The Gravebound Reaper now has a small chance of dropping the Soul-Reaping Scythe. Anything you kill with that scythe has a small chance of dropping its own spawn egg.
Survival gained water infrastructure: pipes, a pump and a tap. The pump draws, the pipes carry, the tap fills. A refrigerator and Spoiled Food arrived with it.
Vehicles gained gasoline. Right-click a vehicle while holding a Gasoline Canister to refuel it. The empty canister does not break — refill it at a crafting table with 4 coal or charcoal.

Power gained an Air Purifier. Running a nuclear plant now pollutes the air around it, and standing in polluted air gives you slowness, then weakness, then poison. A powered purifier clears that pollution locally for as long as it has electricity.

Guns gained a data-driven firearm and attachment system. Put a gun and its attachments into the Gun Workbench and they are fitted the moment you take the gun back out; put a fitted gun back in and they come off. Three guns (Service Pistol, Marksman Carbine, Breaching Shotgun) and six attachments (Red Dot Sight, Suppressor, Extended Magazine, Angled Foregrip, Heavy Stock, Laser Pointer) use it. A Hazmat Suit that blocks nuclear contamination was also added — you need it and the gas mask together.

The Backrooms grew a great deal: Levels 0, 1 and 2, the Poolrooms, the party level and a hub hall lined with numbered doors, plus twelve entities (Hound, Smiler, Faceling, Skin Stealer, Peeling Colossus, Wailing Hulk, Pallid Runner, Partygoer, Deathmoth, Duller, Living Painting, False Puddle) and things to carry — almond water, bandages, a flashlight, a blood test kit, a crowbar, matches.

Building & Decor gained blackout reinforced glass: three shapes (block, pane, plate) in 17 colours. At the same time, the 16 reinforced glass panes that had shipped without a name since v1.7.7 finally got Japanese and English names.

sections.title: Not yet implemented/confirmed at this point
